Anticipating the objections which the Jews might raise as to why God permitted their captivity, and when He did restore them, why He did so by a foreign prince, Cyrus, not a Jew (<reference osisRef="Isa.40.27">Is 40:27</reference>, &c.), but mainly and ultimately, the objections about to be raised by the Jews against God's sovereign act in adopting the whole Gentile world as His spiritual Israel (<reference osisRef="Isa.45.8">Is 45:8</reference>, referring to this catholic diffusion of the Gospel), as if it were an infringement of their nation's privileges; so Paul expressly quotes it (<reference osisRef="Rom.9.4-Rom.8.11">Ro 9:4-8, 11</reference>-<reference osisRef="Rom.8.21">21</reference>).<div eID="gen15667" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15668" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Let ... strive--</hi>Not in the Hebrew; rather, in apposition with "him," "A potsherd among the potsherds of the earth!"
